h: Estuary, cliffs and a comfy seat
p: Exmouth sits where the River Exe meets the sea, and there's plenty to stitch together around a film here. The Exe Estuary Trail is a flat, mostly traffic-free path that's great for walking or cycling, with birdlife on the mudflats and lovely views across the water. Even a short stretch is a nice way to work up an appetite before the trailers.

At the eastern end of the beach, the Geoneedle at Orcombe Point marks the start of the Jurassic Coast World Heritage Site, and the walk up there gives you wide views back across the bay and the red cliffs. It's a bracing little climb, so it's worth doing in daylight before an evening showing.

A short drive out of town, A La Ronde is a quirky sixteen-sided house looked after by the National Trust, and it's a fascinating one for curious minds. Back in town, an easy routine is a beach morning, lunch in the centre, then a film when the little ones need a rest.

Because the cinema is so close to the station, it's a useful option for anyone visiting from Exeter or Lympstone who'd rather not drive, especially on busy summer days when seafront parking fills up. Do keep the subtitled and audio-described showings in mind too, as they're a big help for many families.
